newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Prices close higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Prices close higher.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices ended as much as 5/8 of a point higher Thursday, but one trader said certain segments of the market outperformed others.

"I tell you, it's a two-tiered market developing," the trader said. "The index bonds for sure, and a few real hot names, structured names, are definitely up on the day probably 1/4 or something like that."
The trader was referring to bonds contained in the Bond Buyer's 40-bond index and to other bonds which he described as having "recognizable names" and good call features.
New York City bonds also traded well, he said.
"They are extremely rich, but they've been trading," the trader said. "They are probably up a good 1/4 or so on the day."
A trader of New York paper said while long Cities are somewhat rich, very little in municipals is cheap these days.
"(In) the long end they do seem a little high compared to where they are in 10 years," he said. "The 10-year spread to triple-A is much wider than it is out on the long end."
The trader also cited some trading in City paper.

"There was $10 million sixes of (20)24 that went away, a block of sixes of 2022 traded, (and) sixes of (20)26 got cleaned up," he said. "Part of it is that's what retail is buying because everthing else looks so high to them, and its the only issue that has six percent coupons readily available."

Back in the broader market, a municipal analyst also noticed improvement but cited bigger gains with prices up 3/8 to 5/8 of a point overall. High-grade issues were 3/8 to 1/2 point, while dollar bonds were up 5/8 to more in spots, he said.

The market drew strength both from U.S. Treasury gains and a recent spate of new municipal issues, which helped to define levels, the analyst said. He decribed pricing on those issues as "firm to strong."

On a week-to-week basis, Reuters 10-year tax-exempt general obligation bond index reflected an improved market this week compared to last. The index fell five basis points to 5.17 percent on Thursday versus a reading of 5.22 percent last week.
Calculated each Thursday, the index represents the non-weighted average yield of 15 state and local municipal bonds of 10-year maturity and ratings ranging from A-minus to AAA.
In debt futures Thursday, the December municipal contract was up 11/32 at 112-2/32. The December T-bond contract was up 15/32 at 107-8/32. The MOB spread was 154 ticks.

In the government market, the benchmark 30-year U.S. bond closed up 14/32 at 95-31/32 to yield 7.08 percent. Treasuries got an early boost after the Labor Department said its August Producer Price Index rose 0.3 percent overall and fell 0.1 percent excluding food and energy components. Economists in a Reuters survey expected the data would post 0.1 percent gains in both categories.
In a separate report, initial jobless claims rose to 338,000 in the week ended September 7 from a 317,000 the previous week.
